experiments.protocol_note: The prompt budget is part of the evaluation scope hash. Results at a new budget are not comparable with V4 numbers produced at 512 unless the V4 adapter is re-evaluated under the same budget.
experiments.gate_conclusion: Promptability is a hard prerequisite, not a performance result. 512 fails on both panels. 768 clears val but leaves 28 unpromptable ablation_dev records. 1024 is the smallest tested budget that clears evaluation_panel_fully_promptable on both panels, and 1024+128 leaves ample room in the 2048 sequence budget. Excluding the 28 records to make 768 pass would silently change the panel and is not permitted.

experiments.hypothesis: The policy is undertrained; more verified supervision raises Kill@k.
experiments.result: Quadrupling supervision (553 -> 2,260 examples) moved the selected peak from 70 to 73 of 100, at or barely above the two-function noise floor, while reference-validity still collapsed within the first 50 steps.
experiments.reason: The policy is not data-starved at this learning rate. Scale is not the binding constraint, so further scaling is not the productive lever. Recorded as a negative result: evidence against the undertraining hypothesis that motivated the training-scale ablation.
experiments.prediction_outcome: Both predictions confirmed, recorded before results were viewed: the monitor selected an early checkpoint (50, not terminal 142), and reference-validity at 142 (0.479) ended below step 0 (0.609).
experiments.noise_floor_note: Repeated identical-configuration runs vary by about two functions on this panel at fixed seed. Differences at or below that are not evidence.

experiments.hypothesis: 5e-5 is too aggressive for a 1.5B policy: reference-validity fell while token loss kept improving, which is a learning-rate signature rather than a data-quantity one.
experiments.result: At the selected checkpoint the kill rate is unchanged within noise (72 vs 73) while reference-validity recovers from 0.449 to 0.541 against a 0.609 baseline - roughly 57 percent of the loss 5e-5 caused.
experiments.reason: Section 53 ranks reference-validity above the headline metric, and this buys a large reference-validity gain for no measurable kill-rate cost. Single seed, so directional until confirmed on 43 and 44.
experiments.limitation: A lower rate slowed the degradation but did not prevent it: both arms still peak at the first checkpoint and decline. The learning rate is not the root cause.

experiments.reason: DOWNGRADED from WEAK_ACCEPT. The +4 difference was an unpaired comparison between two separately trained runs on seed 42 alone. metrics.pattern: In every Qwen arm, parse-validity and execution-validity rise monotonically (0.991 -> 0.999 and 0.968 -> 0.991) while reference-validity collapses (0.609 -> 0.43-0.48).

experiments.result: The policy learns to emit well-formed, runnable tests that assert incorrect expected values - it acquires form faster than behaviour. Every arm also peaks at its first monitored checkpoint and declines, so the true maximum has never been observed: a 50-step checkpoint interval is too coarse to locate it.
experiments.reason: Neither more data nor a gentler learning rate fixed this; both only slowed it, which points at supervision content rather than quantity or optimisation speed. Phi-3 is the informative exception: its reference-validity rose under the same recipe, so the collapse is a property of a policy already near its ceiling, not of the recipe. Next: finer checkpointing to locate the peak, and ablation A to test whether the specification is being used at all.

experiments.hypothesis: A smaller code-specialised base model with an available fused-attention backend can raise reference-valid, execution-valid generation and cut generation cost with no change to the evaluation protocol.
evidence_tiers: zero-shot screen on the fixed 32-function panel
trained 200-pair comparison on the 100-function panel, identical 553 records, seed 42, LR 5e-5, 1024 budget

trained_200_pair_comparison_100_function.note: Identical 553 training records (442 synthetic + 111 repository), same seed, same panel, same budget. Only the model differs. The Phi-3 arm is PARTIAL: stopped after step 17, so steps 34 and 35 were never measured.

feasibility.explanation: Phi-3 training is only about nine minutes for the whole run; the cost is monitoring. The same 800-generation monitor pass took 35 minutes at baseline and 7.7 hours mid-training, once optimizer state pushed the card to 98 percent VRAM. Probable cause is allocator thrashing under VRAM exhaustion. This is a hypothesis, not an instrumented diagnosis, and may be a fixable defect rather than a property of Phi-3.

experiments.result: L1 is impossible in the pinned environment. On the trained comparison Qwen leads every candidate-validity layer at the matched checkpoint (parse 0.996 vs 0.749, execution 0.973 vs 0.646, reference 0.580 vs 0.466) while kill rate ties within noise (70 vs 68). But Phi-3 gains far more from the same supervision: +22 functions versus +5, and its reference-validity RISES (0.295 -> 0.466) where Qwen's falls.
experiments.reason: Qwen is adopted as the base model on two grounds. First, quality at matched training: it wins every layer section 53 ranks above the headline metric, with kill rate tied. Second, feasibility: 929 seconds versus a projected 24.5 hours for identical work, which decides whether the remaining programme - roughly fifteen further training runs plus three-seed locked validation and DPO - is a day of GPU or a month.
negative_results_retained: L1 Phi-3 + SDPA: transformers 4.48.3 refuses SDPA for Phi3ForCausalLM and flash-attention does not cover its sliding-window attention. Eager is the only admissible Phi-3 backend here, so no speedup is reachable for the incumbent.

The zero-shot screen OVERSTATED Qwen's advantage. Most of its apparent edge was a head start, not superior trainability: SFT closed the gap from 19 points to 2. A screening result is not a trained result.

Phi-3 was not rejected on merit. It learns more per step and was still improving steeply when stopped. It is set aside because it is impractical on a 24 GB card under the current monitor implementation - a qualified statement, not 'Phi-3 is worse'.
The Phi-3 arm is incomplete: steps 34 and 35 were never measured, so its curve could still have overtaken Qwen's and we would not know.
Repeated identical-configuration runs vary by about two functions at fixed seed; the 70 vs 68 comparison is inside that band.

experiments.hypothesis: Every arm peaked at its first monitored checkpoint (17 at 200 pairs, 50 at 800), so the true maximum had never been observed - only the first place we happened to look. If the real peak sat near step 20 with reference-validity still near 0.58, every recorded number would be an understatement.
experiments.control: the same run at a 50-step interval (M_learning_rate lr_1e-5 arm)
treatments: 10-step interval, early stopping disabled so the whole curve is seen
experiments.protocol_note: Patience was set to 99 so no checkpoint was skipped by early stopping. That changes which checkpoints are observed, never what is measured at each one.

prediction_1.claim: the peak lies strictly before step 50
prediction_1.evidence: The peak is step 60 at 72/100. The best checkpoint strictly before 50 is step 40 at 67, which is worse than the step-50 value of 68 we already had. Steps 10, 20 and 30 (64, 64, 61) are at or BELOW the untrained baseline of 65.

prediction_2.claim: peak reference-validity exceeds the 0.541 measured at step 50
prediction_2.evidence: Reference-validity never rises above its untrained 0.6088. The highest post-training value is 0.6012 at steps 10-20, and those checkpoints kill fewer functions than doing nothing. At the best kill-rate checkpoint (60) reference-validity is 0.5375, LOWER than the 0.541 at step 50.

experiments.result: The coarse 50-step interval was not hiding a better model. Nothing before step 50 beats what was already recorded, so no previous number was an understatement. The peak sits one interval later at step 60 (72/100), worth +4 over step 50 - barely above the two-function noise floor.
experiments.reason: The motivating hypothesis was wrong and is recorded as wrong. Finer checkpointing cost 69 minutes and bought +4 functions at a checkpoint with worse reference-validity than the one it replaces. A 10-step interval is not worth its monitoring cost as a default.
experiments.cross_cutting_confirmation: At 10-step resolution the form-before-behaviour pattern is visible from the FIRST checkpoint rather than emerging later: parse-validity is already climbing at step 10 (0.9912 -> 0.9938) while reference-validity is already falling (0.6088 -> 0.6012). The two metrics move in opposite directions for the entire run. Candidate kill rate rises monotonically to its maximum at the terminal step (0.3175) while function kill rate peaks at 60, so the two success layers do not even peak together.
experiments.practical_consequence: There is no checkpoint that is simultaneously good at killing bugs and faithful to the reference. Selecting on kill rate picks step 60 and accepts reference-validity 0.5375; selecting on reference-validity picks step 10-20 and accepts a kill rate at or below the untrained baseline. This is a genuine trade-off in the current recipe, not a sampling artifact.

experiments.hypothesis: Single-seed conclusions were being judged against a noise floor of about two functions, measured from repeated runs at the SAME seed. If across-seed variability is larger, several accepted findings do not stand.
experiments.changed_variable: random seed only (42, 43, 44); config otherwise identical
experiments.control: seed 42, the seed every prior conclusion rests on

across_seed.statistical_note: Wilson intervals are attached only to per-seed binomial proportions. The across-seed mean is a mean of proportions and is reported with its observed range, never as a binomial sample.

experiments.result: The untrained baseline moves 65 / 58 / 62 across seeds - a range of 7 functions on the same panel with nothing changed but the seed. The previously quoted two-function noise floor was measured at a fixed seed and understates across-run variability by more than threefold. The trained result, by contrast, is 72 / 73 / 73 - a range of 1.

experiments.methodological_correction: Two noise floors apply and were previously conflated. A PAIRED within-seed comparison cancels seed choice, so its floor is same-seed run-to-run variability (about 2 functions). An UNPAIRED comparison between separately trained runs does not, so its floor is the across-seed range (7 functions here). Judging a paired gain against the unpaired range would wrongly discard a real effect; judging an unpaired difference against the paired floor wrongly accepts noise. The earlier single-seed acceptances used the wrong floor.

accepted_changes: M learning rate 5e-5 -> 1e-5 (large reference-validity gain, no kill-rate cost; single seed)
L2 base model -> Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct + SDPA (screening plus trained 200-pair comparison)
SFT itself (paired gains +7/+15/+11 across seeds 42/43/44, and it reduces across-seed variance from a range of 7 to a range of 1)
rejected_changes: I_SCALE 200 -> 800 pairs (peak moved 70 -> 73, within noise; the policy is not data-starved)
L1 Phi-3 + SDPA (infeasible in the pinned transformers/model environment)
N checkpoint-resolution sweep: the understatement hypothesis is refuted; a 10-step interval is not worth its monitoring cost
